observations.why: First-person plural present continuous performs a settled course of action the speaker expects others to join — decision-grade ratification language, not a proposal being argued for.
Flat unhedged assertions presented as justification for the switch — asserted and ready to defend, but the segment offers evidence rather than performing the settling itself; claim, not decision.
The arrow notation records a settled transition as a performed declarative — the memo itself ratifies the migration as decided, not under discussion.
Restates the performance claim as a memo-recorded assertion; the memo reports the claim rather than performing the settling, and no ratification language is present.
A fixed timeline attached to the migration is an operational commitment — the speaker sets a date others are expected to plan around, which is decision-grade rather than a claim being argued.
